title: Ulysses and Argus
about: Home after twenty years and disguised as a beggar, Ulysses is recognized by no one except his old dog Argus, who has waited long enough to see him and no longer. Rivière gives the hero rags and bare feet and lets the dog carry the whole scene.

title: Ulysses and the Sirens
commons_file: WATERHOUSE - Ulises y las Sirenas (National Gallery of Victoria, Melbourne, 1891. Óleo sobre lienzo, 100.6 x 202 cm).jpg
about: Waterhouse paints the Sirens as Homer imagined them, birds with women's heads, circling a ship whose captain has had himself tied to the mast so he can hear them and live.

title: Circe Offering the Cup to Ulysses
commons_file: Circe Offering the Cup to Odysseus (2457 x 4023px ed.).jpg
about: The sorceress holds out the drugged cup that turned his men into swine. Ulysses appears only in the mirror behind her throne, which puts the viewer exactly where he stands.

title: Circe Invidiosa
location: Art Gallery of South Australia, Adelaide
commons_file: J. W. Waterhouse - Circe Invidiosa - Google Art Project.jpg
about: Circe, jealous of the nymph Scylla, pours poison into the sea where her rival bathes. The water turns a sickly green beneath her.

title: Odysseus and Polyphemus
about: The blinded Cyclops heaves a boulder at the escaping ship. Böcklin makes the giant part of the cliff itself.

title: The Magic Circle
about: A sorceress traces a circle of fire around herself with a wand, ravens and a skull outside it. The line on the ground is the painting: inside is power, outside is everything else.

title: Echo and Narcissus
commons_file: John William Waterhouse - Echo and Narcissus - Google Art Project.jpg
about: Narcissus leans over the water, lost in his reflection, while the nymph Echo, who can only repeat others' words, watches him and cannot speak for herself.

title: The Murder of Pelias by His Daughters
about: Medea persuades the daughters of King Pelias that they can make their father young again by cutting him apart and boiling him. They believe her.

title: Clytemnestra
about: The queen stands in the doorway just after killing her husband Agamemnon, axe still in hand, unrepentant.

title: Lady Lilith
about: Lilith, in Jewish legend the first wife of Adam, combs her hair and studies herself in a hand mirror. Rossetti makes seduction look like complete self-possession.

title: The Garden of Armida
about: Tasso's sorceress, who held crusaders captive in an enchanted garden, recast as a modern party: a serious young man in evening dress surrounded by women raising their glasses. A critic at the time asked what he could possibly be expected to do.

title: Faun by Moonlight
about: A faun plays his pipes under a pale moon with goats trailing behind him. Spilliaert, a Belgian Symbolist, makes it feel less like myth than a dream you wake from uneasy.

title: Lady Godiva
about: The legend of the noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry to make her husband lift a cruel tax. Collier paints the moment before, her head bowed.

title: The Ballad of Lenore
commons_file: Musée d'arts de Nantes - 222 - Horace Vernet, La ballade de Lénore, 1839.jpg
about: From Bürger's ballad: a girl who cursed God after her lover died in battle is carried off at night by his ghost on horseback. The dead ride fast.

title: The Passing of Robin Hood
commons_file: N.C. Wyeth - The Passing of Robin Hood.jpg
about: Dying, Robin Hood shoots a last arrow from the window and asks to be buried where it lands. Painted as a book illustration.

title: The Fallen Angel
about: Lucifer just after the fall, arms folded, with a single tear in an eye full of rage. The angels still in heaven drift above him.

title: Lucifer
commons_file: Luzifer (Lucifer) painting by Franz von Stuck 1890 National Gallery in Sofia.jpg
about: A dark figure crouches in shadow and looks straight out of the canvas with glowing eyes. Few paintings of the devil are this quiet or this unsettling.

title: Lucifer in the Giudecca
about: The last circle of Dante's Inferno, where Lucifer is frozen in ice and chews on history's great traitors.

title: Satan Watching the Sleep of Christ
commons_file: Joseph Noel Paton (1821-1901) - Satan Watching the Sleep of Christ - KIRMG-387 - Kirkcaldy Galleries.jpg
about: In the wilderness, Satan stands over Christ as he sleeps. The temptation has not started yet.

title: The Chess Players
about: Satan plays a man at chess with his soul as the stake, while an angel stands behind the man. Chess players have argued for generations over whether the position is really lost.

title: The Wounded Angel
about: Two boys carry an injured angel on a stretcher through a bleak Finnish landscape. Finland voted it the country's national painting in 2006.

title: Watchers in the Night
about: An angel stands guard over a sleeping child, a small flame above one hand.

title: Witches' Sabbath
about: A goat devil presides over a circle of witches who offer him children. Goya was mocking superstition, though the painting outlasts the joke.

title: The Valley of Tears
commons_file: Gustave Doré - La Vallée de larmes.jpg
about: One of Doré's last paintings: Christ with the cross calls to the suffering gathered in a dark valley.

title: Agnus
about: A white lamb stands calm at the center of a ring of snarling wolves, a halo of gold leaf behind it.

title: The Last Supper
commons_file: Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519) - The Last Supper (1495-1498).jpg
about: The moment after Christ says one of them will betray him, and every figure reacts at once. Painted on a wall in an experimental technique that began failing within Leonardo's lifetime.

title: The Sacrifice of Isaac
about: An angel grips Abraham's wrist as the knife comes down, and Isaac screams. Caravaggio refuses to make it serene.

title: Samson and Delilah
about: Samson sleeps in Delilah's lap while a man cuts his hair and soldiers wait at the door.

title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
commons_file: Return of the Prodigal Son 1667-1670 Murillo.jpg
about: The father embraces his son, who has come home with nothing, while servants bring out new clothes and the fatted calf.

title: Belshazzar's Feast
commons_file: John Martin - Belshazzar's Feast - Google Art Project.jpg
about: The writing appears on the wall during the king's banquet, and Martin makes the architecture itself seem to know the empire is finished.

title: Daniel's Answer to the King
commons_file: Daniel's Answer to the King, by Briton Riviere, GMIII MCAG 1937 123-001.jpg
about: Daniel stands with his back to us among the lions, looking up toward the king who put him there. The lions are not the ones afraid.

title: Job and His Friends
about: Job in ruin, visited by the friends who will spend the book explaining why he deserved it.

title: The First Mourning
location: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires
about: Adam and Eve hold the body of Abel, the first human death, and do not yet have a word for what has happened.

title: After the Flood
about: The animals leave the ark and pour down the mountainside into a washed world.

title: Christ of Saint John of the Cross
location: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow
about: Christ on the cross seen from above, hanging over a bay at dawn. Dalí based the angle on a drawing by the sixteenth-century mystic Saint John of the Cross.

title: Napoleon Crossing the Alps
commons_file: Jacques Louis David - Bonaparte franchissant le Grand Saint-Bernard, 20 mai 1800 - Google Art Project.jpg
about: Napoleon on a rearing horse, pointing upward, with Hannibal's name carved in the rock at his feet. He actually crossed on a mule. The painting is propaganda, and knows it.

title: Napoleon and Josephine
about: The emperor and the woman he married, crowned and eventually divorced for failing to give him an heir.

title: The Murder of the Sons of Edward IV
about: Following Shakespeare's Richard III, the two murderers hesitate over the sleeping princes in the Tower. The painting stops time one second before.

title: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan
commons_file: Iván el Terrible y su hijo, por Iliá Repin.jpg
about: The tsar clutches the son he has just struck in rage, blood running through his fingers, horror in his eyes. The painting has been attacked twice.

title: Alexander the Great's Trust in Doctor Philip
commons_file: Alexander the Great's trust in doctor Philip (Siemiradzki) detail02 by shakko.jpg
about: Alexander, gravely ill, drinks the medicine from his physician while handing him a letter accusing that same physician of poisoning him.

title: Alexander the Great Refuses Water in the Desert
about: Crossing the desert with an army dying of thirst, Alexander is offered a helmet of water and pours it into the sand, refusing to drink what his men cannot.

title: The Women of Amphissa
about: After a night of worship, followers of Dionysus wake exhausted in the marketplace of an enemy town, and the town's women quietly protect them.

title: Timoclea Kills the Captain of Alexander the Great
commons_file: Sirani, Elisabetta - Timoclea uccide il capitano di Alessandro Magno - 1659.jpg
about: Timoclea of Thebes pushes the soldier who assaulted her headfirst into a well. Sirani, one of the few women painters of her time, paints the victim as the one in control.

title: The Raft of the Medusa
commons_file: JEAN LOUIS THÉODORE GÉRICAULT - La Balsa de la Medusa (Museo del Louvre, 1818-19).jpg
about: Survivors of the 1816 wreck of the French frigate Méduse, abandoned on a raft for thirteen days, sight a ship on the horizon. A political scandal painted at the scale of history.

title: The Burial of Atala
commons_file: Atala au tombeau - Anne-Louis Girodet - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 4958, louvre 1.jpg
about: From Chateaubriand's novel: a young Native American man and an old priest lower the body of the Christian girl Atala into a cave tomb.

title: Las Meninas
commons_file: Las Meninas, by Diego Velázquez, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg
about: The young princess and her attendants, the painter himself at his canvas, and the king and queen visible only in a distant mirror. Few paintings have been argued over more.

title: Portrait of Juan de Pareja
location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
commons_file: Retrato de Juan Pareja, by Diego Velázquez.jpg
about: Velázquez's portrait of his enslaved assistant, painted in Rome and applauded when shown. Pareja was later freed and became a painter in his own right.

title: The Arnolfini Portrait
about: A couple in their Bruges room, every surface rendered exactly. In the convex mirror behind them two more figures appear, and above it van Eyck signed his name as a witness.

title: Man, Controller of the Universe
location: Palacio de Bellas Artes, Mexico City
about: Rivera's recreation of the Rockefeller Center mural that was destroyed after he refused to paint out Lenin's face.

title: The Black Brunswicker
location: Lady Lever Art Gallery, Port Sunlight
commons_file: John Everett Millais The Black Brunswicker.jpg
about: A woman tries to keep her lover from leaving to fight Napoleon, pressing the door shut while he gently opens it. He will almost certainly not come back.

title: To Arms!
about: A wedding interrupted by the call to war, the groom already turning toward it.

title: God Speed
about: A woman ties her token to the arm of a knight as he rides out to war.

title: The Shadow
about: Before her lover leaves, a woman traces his shadow on the wall, the old story of how drawing began.

title: The Gladiator's Wife
commons_file: Edmund Blair Leighton - The Gladiator's Wife.JPG
about: A woman in the crowd of the arena, watching the fight she cannot bear to watch.

title: A Dream of the Past: Sir Isumbras at the Ford
location: Lady Lever Art Gallery, Port Sunlight
commons_file: John Everett Millais - Sir Isumbras at the Ford (1857).jpg
about: An old knight carries two peasant children across a river at dusk. Mocked by critics at the time, and now among Millais's most loved.

title: The Crown of Love
about: From a Norman legend: a young man must carry his beloved to the top of a mountain to win her, and dies of the effort at the summit.

title: Between Wealth and Love
commons_file: Entre la richesse et l'amour, by William Adolphe Bouguereau.jpg
about: A young woman between two suitors: an older man offering jewels, and a young musician offering himself. She looks at neither.

title: The Awakening Conscience
commons_file: William Holman Hunt - The Awakening Conscience - Google Art Project.jpg
about: A kept woman rises suddenly from her lover's lap as a song reminds her of the life she left. The whole room is a set of clues.

title: The Long Goodbye
about: An intimate farewell between two figures, which Francis has said came from a dream of being sent away by war.

title: Death and the Miser
commons_file: Frans Francken II (1581-1642) - An Allegory of Death and the Rich Man - 959419 - National Trust.jpg
about: Death arrives for a man counting his money. He is still counting.

title: Death and the Maiden
commons_file: La Jeune Fille et la Mort-Marianne Stokes-IMG 8224.JPG
about: The old theme of death coming for a young woman, painted by one of the finest women artists of her generation.

title: Death and the Girl
about: A Belgian painter's version of the meeting every age has painted in its own way.

title: Ophelia
commons_file: John Everett Millais - Ophelia - Google Art Project.jpg
about: Ophelia floats in the stream, singing as she drowns, surrounded by flowers painted leaf by leaf on the riverbank. The model, Elizabeth Siddal, posed in a bathtub.

title: The Scream
about: A figure on a bridge under a blood-red sky, clutching its face. Munch said he felt an infinite scream passing through nature.

title: The Broken Column
about: Kahlo's self-portrait after spinal surgery: her body split open to show a shattered column in place of a spine, nails driven into her skin, her face composed.

title: The Tree of Life
about: A late work by the Surrealist who spent most of her life in Mexico.

title: Laughing Fool
about: A jester grins and peers at us through his spread fingers, the old gesture for folly.

title: The Conjurer
about: A street magician performs cups and balls while an accomplice lifts a spectator's purse. A painting about misdirection, where the audience is the real subject.

title: The Irritating Gentleman
about: A young woman in mourning on a train, a man leaning over the seat to talk at her. She looks straight out at us, as if asking for help.

title: My Wife's Lovers
about: Forty-two cats belonging to a San Francisco millionaire, painted over three years. Among the largest paintings of cats ever made.

title: In a Roman Osteria
about: Two women at a tavern table glance at the viewer while the young man with them sulks. A small comedy of who is interested in whom.

title: A Dear Visitor
about: A sick man in bed raises his hand to greet a visitor he did not expect.

title: Who?
about: A domestic confrontation from the Russian realist, in which the one-word title is the question being asked.

title: At the School Door
about: A barefoot peasant boy in rags stands at the door of a village classroom, looking in at something he wants and cannot have.

title: The Acrobats
about: A family of traveling performers, the mother holding their injured child while the father stands by in costume. The show went on.

title: The Laundress
about: A working woman at her task, from a French painter better known for Belle Époque illustration.

title: At the Dressing Table. Self-Portrait
about: The painter at twenty-four, combing her hair in the mirror on a winter morning. Painted almost in passing, and it made her name.

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
about: A girl turns toward us over her shoulder, lips parted. Not a portrait of anyone known, which is part of why everyone feels they know her.

title: Allegorical Painting of Two Ladies
about: A Black woman and a white woman side by side, both wearing fashionable face patches, above a moralizing inscription. A rare and puzzling double portrait of its time.

title: Never Leave a Red Sock on the Clothesline
about: A giant crimson rabbit looms over two children hiding in a suburban backyard. From Tan's picture book Rules of Summer.

title: The Coward
about: A young woman plants a kiss on a returning soldier who drops his hat and cane in alarm. A Life magazine cover from the end of the First World War.

title: Breaking Home Ties
about: A rancher father and his son wait for the train that will take the boy to college, the son eager, the father already missing him, the dog's head in the boy's lap.

title: Marriage License
about: A young couple signs for their marriage license on tiptoe at the counter while the old clerk sits slumped beside them.

title: After the Prom
about: A teenage couple at a soda fountain, the girl showing her corsage to the soda jerk leaning in to smell it.

title: The Runaway
about: A state trooper at a diner counter talks with a small boy whose bundle of belongings sits on the stool beside him.

title: J. Marion Sims: Gynecologic Surgeon
about: From Thom's series A History of Medicine in Pictures. Sims developed his techniques by operating on enslaved Black women without anesthesia, and the painting has become part of the reckoning with that history.

title: Christina's World
location: Museum of Modern Art, New York
about: Christina Olson, who could not walk, pulls herself across a field toward the farmhouse on the hill. Wyeth's neighbor, painted from behind.
